explanation_en: 'Por causa de' is the standard compound preposition in Portuguese meaning 'because of' or 'due to.' It is essential for B2/C1 learners to master its usage with pronouns and nouns, as it is much more common in speech than 'devido a.'

examples.en_text: We arrived late because of the heavy traffic.
examples.target_text: Chegamos atrasados por causa do trânsito intenso.

examples.en_text: I couldn't sleep well because of the neighbors' noise.
examples.target_text: Não consegui dormir bem por causa do barulho dos vizinhos.

examples.en_text: She decided to move to another city because of her new job.
examples.target_text: Ela decidiu mudar de cidade por causa do novo emprego.

examples.en_text: The flight was canceled because of last night's storm.
examples.target_text: O voo foi cancelado por causa da tempestade de ontem à noite.

examples.en_text: The boss was in a bad mood and, because of that, the meeting was difficult.
examples.target_text: O chefe estava de mau humor e, por causa disso, a reunião foi difícil.

examples.en_text: I had to cancel my plans because of a bad flu.
examples.target_text: Tive que cancelar os meus planos por causa de uma gripe forte.

explanation_en: The expression 'retirar do ar' literally means 'to remove from the air,' referring to pulling a broadcast, show, or website from public viewing or access. It is widely used in media contexts when a program is canceled or suspended. In everyday language, it can also refer to taking down a post or website.

examples.en_text: The television show was taken off the air due to a lack of audience.
examples.target_text: O programa de televisão foi retirado do ar por falta de audiência.

examples.en_text: That controversial interview was taken off the air a few hours after being published.
examples.target_text: Aquela entrevista polêmica foi retirada do ar poucas horas depois de ser publicada.

examples.en_text: The commercial was taken off the air after receiving many complaints from customers.
examples.target_text: O comercial foi retirado do ar após receber muitas reclamações dos clientes.

examples.en_text: Several old channels were taken off the air to make room for new projects.
examples.target_text: Vários canais antigos foram retirados do ar para dar lugar a novos projetos.

examples.en_text: The broadcaster decided to take the series off the air before the end of the season.
examples.target_text: A emissora decidiu retirar o seriado do ar antes do final da temporada.

examples.en_text: If the host keeps talking nonsense, his show will be taken off the air.
examples.target_text: Se o apresentador continuar falando bobagem, o programa dele será retirado do ar.

explanation_en: 'Vamos lá' is an extremely common colloquial expression used to transition to a new topic, start an activity, or encourage someone. It is equivalent to 'let's go' or 'let's get started.' While informal, it is widely accepted in conversational and journalistic settings.

examples.en_text: We are all here now, so let's get started with the meeting.
examples.target_text: Já estamos todos aqui, então vamos lá começar a reunião.

examples.en_text: I know you're afraid of the test, but come on, you can do it!
examples.target_text: Sei que você está com medo do teste, mas vamos lá, você consegue!

examples.en_text: We have a lot of dishes to wash. Let's get to it and get this over with.
examples.target_text: Temos muita louça para lavar. Vamos lá resolver isso de uma vez.

examples.en_text: The car is ready and so are the bags. Let's go before it gets late.
examples.target_text: O carro já está pronto e as malas também. Vamos lá antes que fique tarde.

examples.en_text: The break is over, guys. Let's get back to work.
examples.target_text: O intervalo acabou, pessoal. Vamos lá voltar ao trabalho.

examples.en_text: You said you bought a new phone? Let's go see how it works.
examples.target_text: Você disse que comprou um celular novo? Vamos lá ver como ele funciona.

explanation_en: 'Pegar fogo' literally means 'to catch fire.' Figuratively, it is used to describe a situation, debate, or event that is becoming extremely intense, exciting, or chaotic. It is very common in political and sports commentary.

examples.en_text: The debate between the candidates on television is going to heat up tonight.
examples.target_text: O debate entre os candidatos na televisão vai pegar fogo hoje à noite.

examples.en_text: The party was a bit slow, but when the DJ arrived, the dance floor really heated up.
examples.target_text: A festa estava meio parada, mas quando o DJ chegou, a pista de dança pegou fogo.

examples.en_text: The discussion about the new project really heated up during yesterday's meeting.
examples.target_text: A discussão sobre o novo projeto pegou fogo durante a reunião de ontem.

examples.en_text: With both teams needing the win, tomorrow's game is going to heat up.
examples.target_text: Com os dois times precisando da vitória, o jogo de amanhã vai pegar fogo.

examples.en_text: The competition for first place in the championship is heating up.
examples.target_text: A disputa pelo primeiro lugar no campeonato está pegando fogo.

examples.en_text: When the boss finds out about the mistake, things at the office are going to heat up.
examples.target_text: Quando o chefe descobrir o erro, o escritório vai pegar fogo.

explanation_en: 'Ficar de fora' means to remain on the sidelines, not participate, or be excluded from an activity or event. It is a very common phrasal verb in both informal and formal spoken Portuguese.

examples.en_text: I didn't want to be left out of the trip, so I started saving money.
examples.target_text: Eu não queria ficar de fora da viagem, por isso comecei a economizar dinheiro.

examples.en_text: Since he is still injured, he will have to stay out of tomorrow's game.
examples.target_text: Como ele ainda está lesionado, vai ter que ficar de fora do jogo de amanhã.

examples.en_text: No student should be left out of extracurricular activities.
examples.target_text: Nenhum aluno deve ficar de fora das atividades extracurriculares.

examples.en_text: They decided to have a barbecue over the weekend, but I preferred to stay out of it.
examples.target_text: Eles decidiram fazer um churrasco no fim de semana, mas eu preferi ficar de fora.

examples.en_text: If you don't confirm your attendance soon, you might be left out of the guest list.
examples.target_text: Se você não confirmar sua presença logo, pode ficar de fora da lista de convidados.

examples.en_text: I don't know much about politics, so I prefer to stay out of those discussions.
examples.target_text: Eu não entendo muito de política, por isso prefiro ficar de fora dessas discussões.

explanation_en: 'Dar uma olhada' is the standard colloquial way to say 'to take a look' or 'to check out' something. It is much more common in daily speech than the simple verb 'olhar' when referring to a quick check or review.

examples.en_text: I'm just taking a look at the clothes, thank you.
examples.target_text: Eu só estou dando uma olhada nas roupas, obrigado.

examples.en_text: The boss is taking a look at the report you sent yesterday.
examples.target_text: O chefe está dando uma olhada no relatório que você enviou ontem.

examples.en_text: We are taking a look at some apartments to rent in this neighborhood.
examples.target_text: Nós estamos dando uma olhada em alguns apartamentos para alugar neste bairro.

examples.en_text: The mechanic is already taking a look at your car's engine.
examples.target_text: O mecânico já está dando uma olhada no motor do seu carro.

examples.en_text: Can you wait a minute? I'm still taking a look at the menu.
examples.target_text: Você pode esperar um minuto? Ainda estou dando uma olhada no cardápio.

examples.en_text: I was taking a look at your website and I found the design very modern.
examples.target_text: Eu estava dando uma olhada no seu site e achei o design muito moderno.

explanation_en: 'Valer a pena' is the standard Portuguese equivalent of 'to be worth it' or 'to be worthwhile.' It is constructed with the verb 'valer' (to be worth) and the noun 'pena' (pain, effort, or shame). It can be followed by an infinitive verb or used on its own.

examples.en_text: It's worth visiting the museum in the morning to avoid the queues.
examples.target_text: Vale a pena visitar o museu de manhã para evitar as filas.

examples.en_text: I studied hard for the exam, but it was worth it because I got a good grade.
examples.target_text: Estudei muito para o exame, mas valeu a pena porque tirei uma boa nota.

examples.en_text: Do you think it's worth buying this book or is it better to borrow it?
examples.target_text: Achas que vale a pena comprar este livro ou é melhor pedir emprestado?

examples.en_text: It wouldn't be worth going by car if the traffic is so bad.
examples.target_text: Não valeria a pena ir de carro se o trânsito estiver tão mau.

examples.en_text: Although it's far, I think it's worth going to that beach.
examples.target_text: Embora seja longe, acho que vale a pena ir àquela praia.

examples.en_text: Sometimes, it's worth waiting a bit before making an important decision.
examples.target_text: Às vezes, vale a pena esperar um pouco antes de tomar uma decisão importante.

explanation_en: 'Bora' is a highly popular contraction of 'vamos embora' (let's go). Combined with 'lá', 'Bora lá' is used as an enthusiastic call to action, similar to 'Let's do this!' or 'Let's go!'. It is strictly informal but ubiquitous in Brazil.

examples.en_text: We have a lot to study for tomorrow's exam, so let's do it!
examples.target_text: Temos muito que estudar para o exame de amanhã, por isso bora lá!

examples.en_text: The taxi has already arrived and we don't want to be late. Shall we go?
examples.target_text: O táxi já chegou e não queremos chegar atrasados. Bora lá?

examples.en_text: Do you guys want to try that new restaurant tonight? Let's do it!
examples.target_text: Vocês querem experimentar aquele restaurante novo hoje à noite? Bora lá!

examples.en_text: I know you're tired, but there are only two kilometers left. Come on, let's do it!
examples.target_text: Sei que estás cansado, mas só faltam mais dois quilómetros. Bora lá!

examples.en_text: We already have all the necessary tools to start the project, so let's get to it.
examples.target_text: Já temos todas as ferramentas necessárias para começar o projeto, então bora lá.

examples.en_text: If we clean the house all together, we'll finish faster. Let's get to cleaning this!
examples.target_text: Se arrumarmos a casa todos juntos, acabamos mais rápido. Bora lá limpar isto!

explanation_en: 'Curtir' is a very common colloquial verb meaning 'to enjoy,' 'to like,' or 'to have a good time with.' While it originally meant to tan leather, in modern Portuguese it is the go-to informal verb for liking things, also popularized by social media 'likes' (curtidas).

examples.en_text: I used to really like that band in my teenage years, but now I don't listen to them as much.
examples.target_text: Eu curtia muito aquela banda na minha adolescência, mas agora já não oiço tanto.

examples.en_text: When he was younger, my brother really enjoyed playing soccer in the park with his friends.
examples.target_text: Quando era mais novo, o meu irmão curtia muito jogar futebol no parque com os amigos.

examples.en_text: I used to love going to that beach in the summer because there were almost no tourists.
examples.target_text: Eu curtia muito ir àquela praia no verão porque quase não tinha turistas.

examples.en_text: He really liked that thriller series, but he thought the ending was very weak.
examples.target_text: Ele curtia muito aquela série de suspense, mas achou o final muito fraco.

examples.en_text: I really enjoyed eating at that Italian restaurant near my old job.
examples.target_text: Eu curtia muito comer naquele restaurante italiano perto do meu antigo trabalho.

examples.en_text: My sister used to really enjoy drawing when she was a child, but later she lost the habit.
examples.target_text: A minha irmã curtia muito desenhar quando era criança, mas depois perdeu o hábito.

explanation_en: This informal phrasal verb means to confront, tackle, or go after someone or something aggressively. It is widely used in everyday speech, sports, and political commentary to describe taking decisive action against an opponent or problem. Learners should note that it requires the preposition 'de' (or its contractions) when followed by an object.

examples.en_text: The coach told the team to go after them in the second half.
examples.target_text: O treinador disse para o time ir para cima no segundo tempo.

examples.en_text: She got so angry that she went after him to argue.
examples.target_text: Ela ficou com tanta raiva que foi para cima dele para discutir.

examples.en_text: If we want to win the market, we have to go after our competitors.
examples.target_text: Se nós quisermos ganhar o mercado, temos que ir para cima dos concorrentes.

examples.en_text: When the thief tried to run, the security guard went after him.
examples.target_text: Quando o ladrão tentou correr, o segurança foi para cima dele.

examples.en_text: Don't be afraid of the exam, go tackle it with everything you've got!
examples.target_text: Não tenha medo do exame, vai para cima com tudo!

examples.en_text: They were arguing and I thought they were going to attack each other.
examples.target_text: Eles estavam discutindo e eu achei que eles iam para cima um do outro.

explanation_en: An idiomatic expression meaning to avoid taking responsibility, to back out, or to dodge blame when things go wrong. It literally translates to 'to pull one's body out.' It is very common in informal and journalistic contexts when discussing politicians or public figures avoiding accountability.

examples.en_text: When the boss asked whose fault it was, everyone backed out.
examples.target_text: Quando o chefe perguntou de quem era a culpa, todo mundo tirou o corpo fora.

examples.en_text: You can't just dodge responsibility now that the work has gotten difficult.
examples.target_text: Você não pode simplesmente tirar o corpo fora agora que o trabalho ficou difícil.

examples.en_text: He is always dodging responsibility when we need to clean the house.
examples.target_text: Ele está sempre tirando o corpo fora quando precisamos limpar a casa.

examples.en_text: Whenever there is a problem at the company, the manager washes his hands of it.
examples.target_text: Sempre que há um problema na empresa, o gerente tira o corpo fora.

examples.en_text: If things go wrong, don't try to back out and leave me alone.
examples.target_text: Se as coisas derem errado, não tente tirar o corpo fora e me deixar sozinho.

examples.en_text: They promised to help organize the party, but later they backed out.
examples.target_text: Eles prometeram ajudar na organização da festa, mas depois tiraram o corpo fora.

explanation_en: Originating from the game of snooker (sinuca), where a 'bico' is the corner pocket, this idiom means to be in a very difficult situation with no easy way out. It is equivalent to being 'between a rock and a hard place' or in a 'catch-22.' It is widely used in Brazilian Portuguese across both informal and formal political/economic commentary.

examples.en_text: If I accept the promotion, I'll have to travel a lot; if I refuse, I might get fired. I'm in a real tight spot.
examples.target_text: Se eu aceitar a promoção, vou ter que viajar muito; se eu recusar, posso ser demitido. Estou em uma verdadeira sinuca de bico.

examples.en_text: My sister wants me to go to her wedding, but my best friend is graduating on the same day. What a catch-22!
examples.target_text: Minha irmã quer que eu vá ao casamento dela, mas meu melhor amigo vai se formar no mesmo dia. Que sinuca de bico!

examples.en_text: The company was left in a tight spot when their main client canceled the contract without warning.
examples.target_text: A empresa ficou em uma sinuca de bico quando o principal cliente cancelou o contrato sem aviso prévio.

examples.en_text: He put me in a difficult spot when he asked me if I liked the horrible present he gave me.
examples.target_text: Ele me colocou em uma sinuca de bico quando me perguntou se eu tinha gostado do presente horrível que ele me deu.

examples.en_text: The mayor is in a tight spot: if he raises taxes, he loses votes; if he doesn't, there will be a lack of money for the public works.
examples.target_text: O prefeito está em uma sinuca de bico: se aumentar os impostos, perde votos; se não aumentar, faltará dinheiro para as obras.

examples.en_text: Without a car and with no public transit due to the strike, we were in a tight spot to get to the airport.
examples.target_text: Sem carro e sem transporte público por causa da greve, ficamos em uma sinuca de bico para chegar ao aeroporto.
